clue.text: Recognition of services that artist rejected

indicators.note: rejected here means thrown back, so the word for the artist is read from right to left

parts.note: a drawer is someone who draws, an artist

explanation.surface: An artist turns down an honour offered for their services.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns DRAWER (one who draws) round.
explanation.definitionFit: A payment or prize given in acknowledgement of work done is a recompense for it.

clue.text: Variable income restricts business that could make a profit

indicators.note: restricts means hems in, so the rearranged letters surround the business abbreviation
variable means changeable, so the letters of income are rearranged

parts.note: CO is short for company, a business

explanation.surface: A fluctuating income limits what a firm can earn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Variable' rearranges the letters of income; 'restricts' then holds the business abbreviation inside them, just after the opening letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Something financially viable, able to pay its way, is described this way.

clue.text: Art lover makes a note about unfinished book

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so A plus the note is placed round the shortened book

parts.note: TE is a note of the sol-fa scale

indicators.note: unfinished means the last letter of the book's name is dropped

parts.note: Esther is a book of the Old Testament

explanation.surface: An art enthusiast writes a comment on a novel left incomplete.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfinished' drops the book's last letter; 'about' wraps the article and the sol-fa note round what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone devoted to beauty and the arts is a connoisseur of that kind.

clue.text: Very attractive person possibly met aboard

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters given could be arranged in another way

explanation.surface: Perhaps you could encounter a gorgeous stranger on a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges METABOARD.
explanation.definitionFit: A handsome, desirable man or woman is colloquially called this.

clue.text: The advantage of party official being given assistance

parts.note: a whip is the party official who enforces voting discipline in Parliament
to give a hand is to help

explanation.surface: A political enforcer gains the upper hand when given help.
explanation.definitionFit: Having control or the upper hand over someone is the sense of this phrase.

clue.text: Disconsolate mascot of Sheffield team?

parts.note: the nursery rhyme says the child born on a certain weekday is full of woe, and that weekday names a Sheffield football club

explanation.surface: A sad club mascot at a Sheffield football ground.
explanation.walkthrough: Sheffield Wednesday is an English football club; in the rhyme 'Monday's child', the one born on that day 'is full of woe'.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhyme's woeful child shares a name with the club, so it would be its fitting gloomy emblem.

clue.text: Plain food set before horse

indicators.note: set before means the food word comes first, ahead of the plain word

parts.note: a pie is a kind of food
bald means plain or unadorned, as in a bald statement

explanation.surface: Simple fare put in front of a horse at feeding time.
explanation.definitionFit: A piebald is a horse with black and white patches.

clue.text: Runway where soft breezes move lightly

parts.note: airs are light breezes
to trip is to step nimbly

explanation.surface: A landing strip where gentle winds blow over the grass.
explanation.definitionFit: A strip of ground where aircraft land and take off is a simple airfield.

clue.text: Sleeping place near river for small creature

indicators.note: near means the two pieces sit next to each other, the river following

parts.note: a dorm, short for dormitory, is a room for sleeping
the Ouse is a river in England

explanation.surface: A small animal makes its bed beside a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A small hibernating rodent famous for being sleepy.

clue.text: Measure of alcohol — gets more than one's share of froth on top

parts.note: to hog is to take more than one's fair portion
the head is the foam on top of a poured beer

explanation.surface: Someone greedy with the beer takes most of the foam.
explanation.definitionFit: A large cask, and the liquid quantity it holds, for wine or beer.

clue.text: Porter without a state is still porter

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the drink is wrapped round the state

parts.note: porter is a dark beer
AR is the abbreviation for Arkansas, a US state

explanation.surface: A doorman who has lost his country is still a doorman.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'Porter' is the dark ale, not the carrier; 'without' is used in its old sense of outside.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who carries loads or luggage is a carrier.

clue.text: Somebody returning I admitted to the house, showing friendliness

indicators.note: returning means the word for somebody important comes back, read right to left

parts.note: a nob is a somebody, a person of high standing

indicators.note: admitted to means let into, so I goes inside the word for the house

parts.note: home is the house one lives in

explanation.surface: A notable person comes back and is let into the house, a warm welcome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' reads the word for a somebody backwards; 'admitted to' lets the I into the house word just before its final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Good-natured geniality and warmth towards others.

clue.text: Military display also involves a race

indicators.note: involves means contains, so the word for also wraps round the other pieces

parts.note: too means also
TT is the Tourist Trophy, a motorcycle race on the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: A parade of troops that includes a running contest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involves' places the article and the race inside the word for also; the Isle of Man TT is a famous British motorcycle race.
explanation.definitionFit: An evening military pageant with music and marching, such as the Edinburgh one.

clue.text: We get odd treatment that can damage the user

indicators.note: treatment means handling or processing, so these letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: We receive strange medical care that might harm the patient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'treatment' rearranges WEGETODD.
explanation.definitionFit: A blade sharp on both sides can cut whoever wields it, hence a double-edged argument.

clue.text: Groundless happy feeling about black plant

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the feeling goes round the letter for black

parts.note: euphoria is an intense elation, often unfounded
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: An unjustified sense of joy over a dark-leaved plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts B inside EUPHORIA, after the R.
explanation.definitionFit: The spurges, a large genus of plants with milky sap, are known by this name.

clue.text: Piece of land frequently captured during the crusades

explanation.surface: A field that kept changing hands in medieval holy wars.
explanation.walkthrough: Acre, the port in present-day Israel, was taken and retaken by Crusaders and Saracens.
explanation.definitionFit: An area measure of 4,840 square yards, and also a coastal city that crusaders and Muslims seized repeatedly.

clue.text: Practically — gold, so the saying goes

explanation.surface: Almost precious metal, according to the proverb.
explanation.walkthrough: The saying is 'as good as gold'; the words before 'gold' in it are the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Meaning virtually or nearly, and the phrase that comes before 'gold' in the stock simile for well-behaved children.

clue.text: During break, call up mum

indicators.note: during means within, so the reversed word sits inside the word for break

parts.note: a rent is a tear or break

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word for call is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to cite is to call or summon, as before a court

explanation.surface: Ringing your mother in a lunch break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns the word for call (giving ETIC); 'During' puts that inside the break word after its first letter. 'mum' is not a mother but means silent.
explanation.definitionFit: Keeping quiet, saying nothing, as in keep mum.

clue.text: Recall times Parliament's in recess? On the contrary

indicators.note: Recall says the hidden letters are read backwards
's here means has: the words before it hold the hidden answer

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Bring MPs back while Parliament is on holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: Rather than Parliament being in recess, a recess is in 'times Parliament's', backwards: Recall reverses ESPA.
explanation.definitionFit: A semicircular vaulted recess at the end of a church.

clue.text: Yen invested in foreign capital — that's not characteristic

indicators.note: invested in means put inside, so the yen letter goes into the rearranged word
foreign suggests something strange or altered, so the letters of capital are reworked

parts.note: Y is the abbreviation for the Japanese currency

explanation.surface: Japanese money put into an overseas city is unusual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foreign' rearranges CAPITAL; 'invested in' puts Y into it, third letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Unusual, departing from the norm or type.

clue.text: Thinned out, without hair being cut very short

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the thinning word wraps round the letter

parts.note: to single seedlings is to thin them out
H stands for hair, taken as its initial letter

explanation.surface: Hair thinned out and cropped close by the barber.
explanation.walkthrough: Gardeners 'single' seedlings when thinning them; 'without' (outside) puts SINGLED round H.
explanation.definitionFit: A shingle is a short tapered haircut, so cropped hair is said to be shingled.

clue.text: Underwear, applied, doesn't move

parts.note: stays are an old-fashioned corset
put means applied, as paint put on

explanation.surface: A corset, once on, stays where it is.
explanation.definitionFit: To remain in one place without shifting.

clue.text: Celebrated with uplifting melody and liquid refreshment

parts.note: to sing of something is to celebrate it

indicators.note: uplifting in a down clue means the word for melody is read from bottom to top

parts.note: an air is a tune

explanation.surface: Toasted with a cheering song and a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uplifting' turns AIR into RIA.
explanation.definitionFit: A Spanish punch of red wine, fruit and soda.

clue.text: Pearl originating from oyster reared in eastern native's tank

indicators.note: originating from points to where each of the following words begins, so their initial letters are taken

explanation.surface: A pearl grown from a cultivated oyster kept in a tank in the East.
explanation.walkthrough: Native here is a cultivated oyster.
explanation.definitionFit: A pearl of particularly fine lustre is so called, as the best came from the East.

clue.text: Sound made by a horse shoe without a penny nail

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the shoe word surrounds the other pieces

parts.note: a clog is a wooden shoe
P is the abbreviation for a penny
a pin is a small nail

explanation.surface: A horseshoe missing a penny nail makes a clatter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, so the wooden shoe encloses the penny and the nail.
explanation.definitionFit: The hollow clattering of hooves on a hard road.

clue.text: Dull and uninteresting, holding attention nevertheless

indicators.note: holding means containing, so the dull word wraps round the word for attention

parts.note: a dry subject is uninteresting
to give ear is to pay attention

explanation.surface: Something tedious that still manages to keep an audience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' puts the attention word inside the dull one; 'nevertheless' only adds the surface irony.
explanation.definitionFit: Gloomy, tedious and depressing.

clue.text: One climber endlessly damaged the face of Everest — stupid fellow!

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: damaged means broken up, so the shortened word's letters are rearranged
endlessly means the last letter of climber is dropped
the face of means the front, the opening letter of Everest

explanation.surface: A mountaineer wrecks the north face of the world's highest peak, the idiot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' leaves CLIMBE, which 'damaged' rearranges to MBECIL.
explanation.definitionFit: A fool or idiot.

clue.text: Full day — I consumed dinner early on

parts.note: Sat is short for Saturday
ate means consumed

indicators.note: early on means at the start, so the first letter of dinner

explanation.surface: A satisfying day: I had my main meal early.
explanation.definitionFit: Satisfied to the point of having eaten as much as one wants.

clue.text: Refer a blue (viva voce)

indicators.note: viva voce means by the living voice, spoken, so the words are heard said

parts.note: a blue joke is lewd

explanation.surface: Mention a rude joke in an oral exam.
explanation.walkthrough: A viva voce is also an oral examination, which disguises the instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: To mention or hint at something indirectly.
